name: Vanthorpe Conceal-Carry Vest (Civilian)
description:
A structured vest from Vanthorpe's civilian-grade protective line, cut to read as a clean technical layer — something you might wear over a shirt in a business-casual or field environment without drawing attention. The outer face is a matte-finish synthetic in charcoal, navy, or black, with four external utility pockets sized for transit cards, personal devices, and documentation. The interior is where the work is: two body armor panels in Vanthorpe's Gen-4 flexible ballistic composite, rated for low-velocity projectile and blade resistance at standard concealed wear gaps. The panels are removable for cleaning.

This is not military-grade. Vanthorpe is careful to call it 'protective,' not 'armored.' It's legal to own in GLMZ under civilian carry ordinances, and it's popular enough that it reads as ordinary technical fashion rather than a threat indicator — which is entirely the point. It's worn by private couriers, licensed investigators, mid-level fixers, and anyone who moves through mixed-tier environments professionally and wants a quiet edge.
functionality: Removable body armor panels rated for low-velocity projectile resistance and blade-edge protection. Does not cover arms or shoulders. No electronics. Panels are Gen-4 flexible ballistic composite — protective but not military-grade.
what_it_says: You go places where being careful is the right call, and you're experienced enough to be careful without looking like it. This isn't paranoia — it's professional preparation.
story_hooks: A recent change in GLMZ's civilian carry ordinance is being lobbied by Ouroboros Legal Division — the new language, if passed, would require registration of any garment with ballistic-rated materials, effectively creating a database of everyone who owns one.
A Vanthorpe Conceal-Carry Vest was left behind at a crime scene with the armor panels removed — someone took the protection out of it before the incident, which suggests they knew what was coming.
Vanthorpe has a known secondary market problem: counterfeit versions with non-rated panels that look identical but provide no actual protection, sold at a discount in Tier 2 markets.

physical_description.visual_profile: A streamlined technical vest with a minimalist aesthetic. Sits close to the torso without bulk, designed to layer cleanly under or over a shirt. The structured silhouette reads as professional-casual rather than tactical—no obvious webbing, straps, or combat styling. Sharp vertical lines from the pocket placement create an elongated frame.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not restrictive; allows full range of motion through the shoulders and arms. Cut to accommodate light layering without gapping. The waist is gently suppressed to maintain a clean line. Not compression-tight, but intentionally contoured to avoid the baggy 'gear vest' look.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte-finish synthetic ballistic composite exterior (likely recycled polymer blend). Interior features removable Gen-4 flexible ballistic panels in high-density aramid-equivalent weave. Panels are stealthy and designed not to show through standard business wear.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost suede-like matte finish on the outer face. Panels have a subtle ribbed texture for grip and structural integrity. Zipper tracks and seams are clean and flush. No visible stitching on external surfaces—professional finish.
physical_description.color_scheme: Available in charcoal, navy, or black. All options have a slight UV-matte treatment that absorbs rather than reflects light. Discreet tonal accent stitching at seams. No branding visible from the front.
physical_description.closures: Center front full-length YKK industrial zipper with internal wind guard. Four external utility pockets with magnetic snap closures (silent operation). Removable armor panels secured with medical-grade velcro and discrete retention tabs.
distinctive_features: Four external utility pockets precisely sized for transit cards, personal devices, documentation—purposefully shallow to avoid bulk
Removable Gen-4 ballistic composite panels rated for blade and low-velocity projectile resistance
Interior ventilation mesh panels for extended wear comfort
Discreet RFID-blocking material integrated into front panels
Tonal Vanthorpe embossed logo on interior neckline only—no external branding
Invisible anchor points for optional shoulder harness mounting (professional use)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 crossover. Expensive enough to signal legitimate protective investment (Tier 2 professional), but marketed and worn by working-class couriers and fixers (Tier 3). Deliberately positioned as practical rather than luxury.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by licensed investigators, private couriers, fixers navigating mixed-tier zones, corporate field operatives, and anyone moving through uncertain environments professionally. Signals competence and preparedness without drawing hostile attention. Normalized enough in GLMZ that it reads as technical fashion rather than threat.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new, with a slight sheen breaking in after 50-100 hours of wear. Panels maintain structural integrity indefinitely if cared for. External surface shows minimal wear—matte finish hides marks well. Discoloration more likely around pocket edges from repeated access.
